title: Rom 8:30: learned Protestants include sanctification under justification
source_text: VIII. Imo in ipsis Paulinis Epistolis reperiuntur quaedam loca ubi viri inter Protestantes doctissimi & celeberrimi, existimant justificari non esse simpliciter in judicio divino absolvi, & pronunciari justum, sed sanctum & justum effici per Spiritus Sancti innovationem: Ejusmodi est celebris ille locus qui legitur Rom. 8. vers. 30. Quos praedestinavit, hos & vocavit; & quos vocavit, hos & justificavit; quos autem justificavit, hos & glorificavit. Cum enim ibi Paulus catenam quandam texat divinorum beneficiorum, quorum sumus per Christi gratiam participes, ab ipsa nostra praedestinatione, usque ad gloriam illam quam in coelis expectamus, nullo modo videtur omissurus fuisse illud singulare atque praecipuum, quo, scilicet liberamur a peccati servitute, & vera sanctitate & justitia nobis inhaerente donamur; neque tamen illius distinctam & expressam mentionem facit. Unde sequitur illud comprehendi sub aliquo beneficiorum ab Apostolo enumeratorum. Ad nullum autem convenientius revocari potest quam ad justificationem, quam plerique Theologi agnoscunt gratiam istam quandoque in Scriptura connotare atque includere. Quod enim dicunt quidam eo loci Paulum sanctificationem sub glorificatione complecti, durum est atque alienum, nec congruit stylo & usui Scripturae, ex qua nullus omnino potest proferri locus, in quo glorificare sit sanctitate & justitia donare.
pass_a_gloss: Nay, in the Pauline Epistles themselves certain places are found where the most learned and celebrated men among Protestants think that to be justified is not simply to be absolved in the divine judgment and pronounced just, but to be made holy and just by the renewal of the Holy Spirit: of this kind is that famous place which is read in Rom. 8:30. Whom he predestined, those he also called; and whom he called, those he also justified; and whom he justified, those he also glorified. For since there Paul weaves a certain chain of divine benefits of which we are partakers through the grace of Christ, from our very predestination unto that glory which we await in heaven, in no way does he seem about to have omitted that singular and chief benefit by which we are freed from the slavery of sin and gifted with true holiness and righteousness inhering in us; and yet he makes no distinct and express mention of it. Whence it follows that it is comprehended under some one of the benefits enumerated by the Apostle. But to none can it more conveniently be referred than to justification, which most theologians acknowledge that grace sometimes to connote and include in Scripture. For what some say, that in that place Paul embraces sanctification under glorification, is harsh and alien, nor does it agree with the style and usage of Scripture, from which no place at all can be produced in which to glorify is to gift with holiness and righteousness.
pass_b_english: Rom 8:30: some top Protestants read justify as Spirit-wrought making holy, not bare acquittal.
Inhering holiness must sit somewhere in the chain; stuffing it under glorify is forced.

choices.why: Wider Pauline benefit, not only forensic.
